summary: The change does what part 1 asked for. `LandingCommit` now has a required `kind`, a snake_case enum with exactly `job_landing`, `declared_intervention` and `records_only`. It keeps `deny_unknown_fields`. `job` and `verification` are now optional and left out of the JSON when absent. `Landing::validate` calls a new per-commit check: a `job_landing` commit must carry both `job` and `verification`, and the other two kinds may carry neither. New tests cover all of this: each kind round-trips through JSON, and an unknown kind, a missing kind or an unknown field fails to parse. The one builder in gh.rs, `commits()`, now sets `job_landing` with `job` and `verification`, and its landing test passes. land.rs, which holds `pr_commits`, is untouched. I ran `cargo test -p athena-data history` (17 passed) and `cargo test -p athena-core gh` (60 passed, plus 1 in the external-calls guard). The fmt, clippy and full test records Athena took on this tree all passed. manage.rs was on the planned list but did not change. That is not a problem: it only passes the commits through, and no criterion depends on it. I found no changes outside the planned list, no secrets and no broken defaults.
